verdict.rationale: Fellow's own REST API covers a meaningful slice of the UI's core objects: it reads notes, recordings and transcripts, writes note agendas in round-trippable Fellow Markdown, completes and archives action items, uploads recordings, and deletes notes (super admin only). Nothing documents parity for workspace settings, recording and retention policies, keyword tracking, transcript redaction, bot customization or Ask Fellow, so 'everything in the UI' is not shown. missing for 10: evidence of API coverage for admin and workspace settings, recording/retention policy configuration, Ask Fellow, and other UI-only features; non-admin note deletion; a stated API-parity commitment; independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note.
The format round-trips: the `content_fellow_markdown` you read from a note is exactly what you can send back to `POST /note/{id}/agenda`.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
Only users with super admin privileges can delete notes through the API.
